title: NoviHealth - safety degradation handoff + mitigations
summary: Post-incident handoff for conversational safety regression that caused elevated fail-open responses during weekend traffic spike. Reviewed root cause hypothesis (tokenization mismatch + model fallback mis-route), agreed on immediate mitigations (short-term model pin, tightened fallback policy, extra canary), and scheduled reliability experiments and security review for KMS and audit logging cadence.
action_items: Priya - run KV cache eviction stress test and share results - 2026-12-08
Tom - provide example inputs that triggered safety drift - 2026-12-05
Luca - send pilot pricing and dedicated capacity options doc - 2026-12-09
Aisha - schedule security questionnaire review with Redwood SRE - 2026-12-10
next_steps: Redwood to pin model version and push canary to 10% traffic by 2026-12-06
Customer to run replayed request set and share false-positive/negative list by 2026-12-05
Joint runbook update session next Wed 2026-12-09 16:00 UTC
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-03 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~59m | Attendees: Evan, Priya, Luca / Rosa, Tom, Aisha, Ben

00:00:05 Evan: Okay, thanks everyone for hopping on. This is Evan from Redwood, I'm the AE; Priya and Luca are here with me. Rosa, Tom, you had forwarded the postmortem draft, we read through it, thanks.
00:00:18 Rosa: yeah thanks, sorry this weekend was rough, um we saw the model start returning what our support folks called permissive answers, like policy bypass, and it correlated with the autoscale burst on sunday morning.
00:00:30 Priya: right uh quick note, transcription maybe: when you say permissive, do you mean the safety classifier threshold was being ignored or the fallback path returned a smaller model with different safety tuning?
00:00:42 Rosa: we think fallback path, but there may also be tokenization mismatch. Ben's got examples.
00:01:05 Ben: hi, yes, I uploaded a small sample to the shared folder, link in the notes. the pattern is mid-conversation the tokens got split, and the KV cache hit was high so a cached context from an older conversation got prefixed. so the system sometimes saw a partially sanitized prompt.
00:01:30 Priya: okay that's interesting, K V cache prefixing interacting with tokenization, we have seen that in other clients but usually not with safety drift. It can cause context bleed if prefix eviction isn't aggressive.
00:01:46 Tom: just to add we were using the hosted endpoint with autoscaling defaults during the spike. No dedicated capacity. also we were on the latest recommended model tag, but Redwood's fallback chain pushed a smaller quantized variant when load hit X.
00:02:10 Evan: right which is the crux. Our smart routing will fall back to a lighter weight variant when latency SLOs at that tier are threatened. In your config, the fallback policy was permissive - allow any compatible variant. That meant a model with a different safety fine-tune got routed for some requests.
00:02:30 Rosa: would you call that a configuration bug or expected behavior?
00:02:36 Evan: expected behavior but the policy should be tighter for safety-sensitive workloads. We should have flagged that in the runbooks.
00:02:47 Luca: and to add, our model catalog metadata sometimes has the safety profile label, but in older model variants that label was missing or mis-named (e.g., "safety-lite" vs "safety-v1"), so the router couldn't always discriminate.
00:03:05 Aisha: that's worrying from an audit standpoint. We need assurance that fallback choices are logged and can be traced for each request. Also KMS rotation and usage logs are needed.
00:03:20 Priya: we do emit model_variant and routing_decision in trace metadata, but I agree we need to make the auditing more visible in your console. Luca can pull the traces for sample requests.
00:03:35 Luca: yes I can. quick aside, the traces are in the dev project by default; I'll share a link. expect some noise in the logs because of the autoscaling churn.
00:04:00 Tom: one more data point: when the fail-open happened, latency percentiles spiked then dropped when fallback activated. So there's a narrow window where the smaller model responded faster but with different safety guardrails.
00:04:18 Evan: ok so hypothesis: tokenization split + KV/prefix caching + permissive fallback policy + missing safety label on fallback variant -> safety regression under scale.
00:04:36 Rosa: sounds right to me.
00:04:42 Priya: immediate mitigation I propose: 1) pin the model to the currently verified safety variant for all safety-sensitive routes; 2) tighten fallback to only allow variants with explicit safety profile header; 3) make prefix cache eviction more aggressive for these routes.
00:05:00 Ben: can prefix eviction be route-specific? we have hybrid workloads so not everything needs that cost.
00:05:08 Priya: yes, eviction policy is configurable per route; we can set smaller cache windows for safety routes.
00:05:20 Rosa: timeline wise we need an action within 48 hours or we'll keep risk over the holiday period.
00:05:29 Evan: agreed. We can pin the model and tighten fallback today, and push a canary by Monday to 10% traffic.
00:05:37 Tom: do you have any risk that pinning will increase latency or cost?
00:05:43 Evan: depends if the pinned model is heavier - but since the issue was the lighter variant causing safety drift, the pinned model should be the verified safety model; we can add a small burst reserve to keep latency in range. Our dedicated option could help but that's a longer procurement path.
00:06:00 Aisha: security asks: full audit trail of model selection for each request, and KMS rotation evidence. Also SOC2 requirements around change management.
00:06:12 Luca: we can add model_selection events to your existing audit logs and add a daily digest for the next two weeks while we monitor. KMS usage is already in the key manager logs; we'll coordinate with your security team to show rotations.
00:06:30 Rosa: thanks. Also, is there a way to run a replay of the weekend traffic against the pinned config?
00:06:38 Priya: yes, Redwood supports replay tooling — you can export the request batch and we can run it against a pinned model in a sandbox, we record responses and give you diffs for safety classifiers.
00:06:50 Ben: I already exported a subset, link in the notes.
00:06:56 Priya: perfect. We'll run that with stricter prefix eviction and fallback guardrails.
00:07:10 Evan: ok let's map responsibilities. Priya will run KV/cache stress tests and run the replay. Luca will push the canary and add audit logging. Evan will coordinate pinning. Aisha will validate with security. Tom will provide additional examples.
00:07:28 Rosa: can we also look at long-term: model labeling hygiene in the catalog and automated gating for safety variants?
00:07:36 Luca: yes, we have a labeling audit job we can run weekly; we can also add an automated gating rule so fallback doesn't pick unlabeled variants. It's a config change in the router.
00:07:50 Tom: what's the rollback plan if the canary shows unexpected regressions?
00:07:54 Priya: auto-rollback to previous routing with circuit-breaker if error rate or safety mismatches exceed threshold. We'll set conservative thresholds for the first canary.
00:08:06 Aisha: data residency: some of these requests contain PHI, so if we need to use a sandbox you must guarantee no external model training and that logs are in-region.
00:08:18 Evan: understood, we will run the sandbox inside your region and ensure logs are flagged as non-training. We'll put that in the pact.
00:08:26 Rosa: okay good. I want to make sure we capture the longlist of mitigations and what is temporary vs permanent.
00:08:34 Evan: agreed. Temporary: pin model, tighten fallback, aggressive eviction. Medium-term: catalog labeling, gating rules, additional canary runners. Long-term: consider dedicated capacity or priority pool for safety-critical traffic.
00:08:50 Ben: any notes on quantization? the fallback variant was quantized and maybe had different tokenization behavior.
00:08:58 Priya: quantization can affect token embeddings and occasionally safety guard signals if model was fine-tuned differently. We'll include quantization parity checks in the replay.
00:09:14 Tom: let's talk about monitoring: we need a safety metric — like safety_score drop rate — surfaced as an alert in your console and our pager.
00:09:22 Luca: we can add a safety regression alert powered by your eval harness; threshold you pick. Also we can stream an event to your pager on model_variant change.
00:09:32 Aisha: please ensure events include request id, model_variant, region, and KMS key id.
00:09:38 Priya: noted. We'll include that payload.
00:09:44 Evan: jump ahead a bit, here's the concrete schedule we recommend: today pin + fallback config; by 2026-12-05 run replay and provide false-pos/neg list; by 2026-12-06 deploy canary; 2026-12-09 joint runbook update and security questionnaire review.
00:10:02 Rosa: that timeline works. will the pinning be reversible?
00:10:07 Evan: yes reversible and auditable.
00:10:12 Tom: curious about cost, if we pin heavier model, can you estimate delta?
00:10:18 Luca: we have a quick model-cost estimator; I'll run it for your traffic profile and share an expected percent change. Expect a small increase but offset by fewer safety incidents.
00:10:28 Ben: on the runbook — we needed clearer guidance on when to declare an incident vs an ops blip; can we jointly author that section?
00:10:36 Luca: absolutely, we'll co-author a short incident decision tree and attach to your ops runbook.
00:10:44 Evan: ok I'll own the postmortem document updates, Priya will own technical validation, Luca will own runbook and logs, Aisha will own security signoff.
00:10:56 Rosa: sounds good, thanks.
00:11:05 -- brief silence as folks scan docs --
00:15:00 (conversation continues, deeper technical dive)
00:15:12 Priya: I dug into the cache telemetry. There's a correlation between high prefix hit ratio and older conversation contexts being applied. A race during cache refills under heavy load can keep stale prefixes. We'll add a TTL enforcement.
00:15:33 Tom: can TTL be fractionally less for safety routes?
00:15:37 Priya: yes parameterizable per route.
00:15:42 Ben: also we saw a handful of examples where the tokenizer produced an extra control char — maybe an encoding mismatch from mobile clients — that looked like a prompt injection vector.
00:15:55 Aisha: that sounds like client-side sanitization gap. we'll push a patch to the mobile team.
00:16:02 Rosa: would mobile clients be sending different content-length or encoding?
00:16:06 Ben: some clients used latin-1 fallback in the weekend build, so yes. we have a ticket to standardize.
00:16:15 Evan: action to ensure client encoding normalized before sending; we can also add server-side normalize as a defense-in-depth.
00:16:24 Luca: adding to notes.
00:20:00 (mid-call status checks and small interruptions)
00:20:10 Priya: regarding the router labels, we will implement a hard deny in the router if safety_profile metadata is missing — until label hygiene job finishes. That prevents unlabeled variants from being selected as fallbacks.
00:20:28 Rosa: that feels like a good short-term hardening.
00:20:33 Tom: how will that affect capacity if many variants are unlabeled?
00:20:38 Priya: it could reduce available fallback candidates, so we will open a temporary burst pool to cover capacity. This is a config-level soft reserve, not a long procurement.
00:20:50 Evan: also we can enable request-level throttling so spikes degrade gracefully instead of switching model families.
00:21:00 Aisha: audit wise, how soon can we get a log export showing model_variant per request?
00:21:05 Luca: same day — I'll share a query and schedule an export job for the last 72 hours.
00:21:12 Tom: great.
00:25:00 (questions about legal/comms)
00:25:10 Rosa: our legal team asked if we should notify customers — we had some user complaints. do you have guidance on incident comms?
00:25:19 Evan: we can help draft a template. since this affected partial subset for a short window, recommended comms include what happened, what we've done, and what steps are ongoing; coordinate with your legal. Luca will provide an incident timeline export.
00:25:32 Rosa: perfect.
00:30:00 (operational knobs and reliability experiments)
00:30:05 Priya: for reliability experiments we'll run: A) prefix-ttl reduction trial, B) labeled-only fallback gating, C) replay with quant-parity check. Each experiment will have metrics: safety_score, latency p95, cost delta.
00:30:23 Ben: can we get a dashboard with those three panels?
00:30:27 Luca: yes, we can spin up a shared dashboard.
00:30:33 Tom: timeline for experiments?
00:30:36 Priya: run replay and TTL test in next 48 hours; gating and canary by Monday; dashboard ready by 2026-12-07.
00:30:45 Rosa: noted.
00:40:00 (discussion drifts to long-term procurement)
00:40:10 Rosa: we also want to evaluate Redwood Dedicated. If we had reserved capacity for safety routes, would fallback risk reduce?
00:40:20 Evan: yes, Dedicated gives you isolation and predictable throughput; router still has fallback but you can keep a hot pool of verified variants. We can show a cost/benefit with your traffic pattern.
00:40:32 Tom: SE question: would dedicated help with the KV cache correctness or just capacity?
00:40:38 Priya: primarily capacity and isolation; cache correctness is more about eviction policy and implementation. However, with dedicated you have more control over kernel and runtime settings.
00:40:50 Aisha: procurement timeline?
00:40:52 Luca: we'll share options and typical lead times; Dedicated sometimes needs contract sign-off but we have expedited paths for safety customers.
00:41:05 Rosa: ok please include that in the materials.
00:45:00 (wrap-up and recap)
00:45:12 Evan: quick recap: immediate items - Redwood to pin model and tighten fallback (Evan/Luca/Priya), run replay and tests (Priya), share logs and timeline (Luca), customer to provide example inputs and security validation (Tom/Aisha). We'll run canary and monitor safety_score.
00:45:35 Rosa: and then joint runbook update on 2026-12-09.
00:45:40 Evan: yes. If anything changes we notify via the incident channel.
00:46:00 (some cross talk)
00:46:18 Priya: one more technical note: we'll enable a temporary request header check that forces route-specific TTL and bypasses prefix reuse for one-turn sessions. That reduces blast radius.
00:46:35 Ben: okay good.
00:50:00 (final Q&A)
00:50:05 Aisha: will you also run a security posture audit for the canary sandbox?
00:50:10 Luca: yes, short checklist: KMS usage, in-region processing, non-training flag, and log retention. We'll send a checklist.
00:50:20 Tom: I'm assigning an ops lead internally to be on-call for the canary window.
00:50:25 Rosa: thanks everyone, let's keep tight comms.
00:50:35 Evan: thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the pinned config change.
00:50:42 (meeting ends)

Post-call notes: pinned model version successfully staged later that day, canary scheduled for 2026-12-06 09:00 UTC. Replay run started 2026-12-04 02:00 UTC.
